Words to review: %1$d. It takes just a couple of minutes!

The app uses spaced repetition. A word you answered well comes back later and later (10 minutes, 1 day, 4 days, weeks, months). A word you forgot comes back soon. This way you spend time only on words that are about to fade from memory.

Words are sorted by how common they are in real speech. The first level holds the ~500 most frequent words; the next ones (A2, B1, B2, C1, C2) hold rarer and rarer words. A few thousand words from levels A1–B2 are already enough for everyday conversation. Start with A1 and move up.
What appears in a session, and in what order

1) First come the words that are due for review: you have already met them and it is time to repeat them.\n2) Then come new words, up to your daily limit (Settings → Workload).\nA wrong answer returns the word to the same session a few cards later, until you get it right. The progress bar counts words, not attempts.

• Learn + review — the normal mode: due words first, then new ones.
• Due only — repeat what is scheduled, without new words.
• Practice — extra training on words you have already learned, in random order. It does not change the schedule, so it is safe for cramming before a trip or an exam.
• Hard words — the words you got wrong most often. Also does not change the schedule.

• Cards — you see a word; try to recall the translation, tap “Show answer”, then rate yourself.
• Choice — pick the right translation out of four.
• Typing — type the translation, or tap the microphone and say it. A new dictation replaces the previous text until you press “Check”.
• Listening — you hear the word and write it down. Great for pronunciation and spelling.

• Show answer — flips the card (tapping the card works too).
• Again / Hard / Good / Easy — how well you remembered the word. The time under each button shows when the word will return: Again = soon (about 10 minutes), Easy = much later. Be honest: the schedule adapts to you.
• Swipe — after flipping, swipe right if you knew the word, left if you did not.
• Speaker icon — pronounces the word. “Sentence” pronounces the example sentence, so you can hear the word in real speech.
• Already know — removes the word from learning for good.
Browse and search all words. Tap an example sentence to hear it. ★ adds a word to favorites; ✓ marks it as known — it will no longer appear in sessions.

The daily goal is the number of answers you aim for each day. The streak counts the days in a row with at least one answer. The daily limit of new words protects you from overload: you can switch it off in Settings, or tap “Learn 10 more new words” at the end of a session.

The interface language and the language you are learning are two separate settings. Russian speakers learn English; English speakers learn Russian. The words of the language you are learning are pronounced aloud and recognized by voice. Settings → Card direction chooses whether you see the learned language first, your own language first, or a mix. Pronunciation and voice input need the Android voice for that language (install it in Android settings if you hear nothing).
A little every day beats a lot once a week. Do the reviews first. Do not be afraid of “Again” — that is how the app learns what you need.
